records.source_label: In Puget Sound and approaches in Haro Strait, Boundary Pass and in the Strait of Georgia
records.official_name: In Puget Sound and its approaches in Haro Strait, Boundary Pass and in the Strait of Georgia
records.tss_identity_note: IMO name as amended by COLREG.2/Circ.55 (MSC 79, 15 December 2004; amendments implemented 1 July 2005). US statutory text splits it into 33 CFR 167.1320-1323 (Puget Sound and its approaches) and 167.1330-1332 (Haro Strait, Boundary Pass, Strait of Georgia). Grouped heading; the separate Strait of Juan de Fuca and approaches schemes (33 CFR 167.1300/1310) are not part of this label.
grouped_components: Approaches to Puget Sound other than Rosario Strait
records.vts_relationship_basis: US parts: 33 CFR 161.55 defines the VTS Puget Sound area as US navigable waters of the Salish Sea to the US/Canada boundary, and Table 161.12(c) assigns Seattle Traffic Ch 14 (Puget Sound) and Ch 5A (US Salish Sea incl. Rosario Strait and US side of Haro Strait). Canadian parts: CCG RAMN 2026 Table 3-1 places Canadian waters through Haro Strait, Boundary Pass and the Strait of Georgia in Victoria VTS Zone Sector 1 (Victoria Traffic Ch 11). Both operate within the US/Canadian CVTS; the CVTS northern limit is 49°N, so the Strait of Georgia component north of 49°N is a Canadian-only VTS area.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: No IMO-adopted (SOLAS V/11) mandatory ship reporting system found for this area. 33 CFR 161 VMRS reporting (sailing plans, position and final reports) applies, but it is the ordinary participation duty of the VTS and is recorded with the service, not as a separate reporting system. A failed search does not establish absence. Canadian side: Vessel Traffic Services Zones Regulations (SOR/2025-275, replacing SOR/89-98) require sailing plans, including a 24-hour report when entering from outside Canadian waters; again VTS participation reporting.
records.applicability_notes: US: VMRS users per 33 CFR 161.16 (power-driven 40 m+, towing vessels 8 m+, passenger vessels certificated for 50+). Eastern San Juan Island Archipelago VTS Special Area rules (Rosario Strait) for vessels 100 m+ / 40,000 DWT+. Canada: vessels 300 GT+, tows 500 GT+ combined, pollutant/dangerous goods carriers; some provisions also to vessels 20 m+ (RAMN s3.5.1).
records.complexity_reason: Cross-border grouped scheme under two national VTS regimes within the CVTS, with sector-specific frequencies and a VTS Special Area.
records.open_questions: Confirm whether 33 CFR 161.55 reference to a Vancouver centre is obsolete (RAMN 2026 lists Victoria Traffic only). SOR/2025-275 full text not fetched (only the SOR/89-98 repeal note).
records.research_effort: approx 7 web actions (eCFR parts 161/167 via API, NAVCEN, RAMN 2026, Justice Laws, IMO compilation)

records.source_label: Off San Francisco
records.official_name: Off San Francisco
records.tss_identity_note: 33 CFR 167.400-406: six parts (Precautionary Area, Northern, Southern and Western Approaches, Main Ship Channel, Area To Be Avoided). IMO adoption circular not separately retrieved.
records.vts_relationship_basis: 33 CFR 161.50 VTS area includes seaward approaches within a 38 nm radius of Mount Tamalpais. Table 161.12(c) expressly includes the San Francisco Offshore Precautionary Area (Ch 14) and the offshore waters within 38 nm (Ch 12). All 33 CFR 167.401-406 coordinates lie within about 30 nm of Mount Tamalpais (computed), so the whole scheme is within the VTS area.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: No IMO-adopted (SOLAS V/11) mandatory ship reporting system found for this area. 33 CFR 161 VMRS reporting (sailing plans, position and final reports) applies, but it is the ordinary participation duty of the VTS and is recorded with the service, not as a separate reporting system. A failed search does not establish absence.
records.voluntary_reporting: Offshore Vessel Movement Reporting System (OVMRS), operated by VTS San Francisco; NAVCEN states it is completely voluntary (existing register SRS-008).
records.applicability_notes: VMRS users per 33 CFR 161.16 (power-driven 40 m+, towing vessels 8 m+, passenger vessels certificated for 50+).
records.complexity_reason: Single VTS covers the whole scheme, but two sectors/frequencies and a separate voluntary offshore reporting system.
records.open_questions: OVMRS geographic extent not stated on NAVCEN page; not confirmed whether it extends beyond the 38 nm VTS area.

records.source_label: In the Santa Barbara Channel and in the Approaches to Los Angeles - Long Beach
records.official_name: In the Santa Barbara Channel; In the approaches to Los Angeles-Long Beach
records.tss_identity_note: Grouped heading of two schemes: Santa Barbara Channel (33 CFR 167.450-452, Point Vicente to Point Arguello) and approaches to Los Angeles-Long Beach (33 CFR 167.500-503: precautionary area, western and southern approaches). IMO compilation shows later amendments to both (Santa Barbara Channel amended scheme; 'Approaches to Los Angeles - Long Beach' amended scheme), circular numbers not extracted.
grouped_components: In the Santa Barbara Channel (Point Vicente to Point Conception; Point Conception to Point Arguello)
In the approaches to Los Angeles-Long Beach (precautionary area, western approach, southern approach)
records.vts_relationship_basis: Partial coverage only. LA/LB approaches: 33 CFR Table 161.12(c) VMRS area (San Pedro Traffic) is 25 nm radius of Point Fermin Light; the precautionary area and western approach lie wholly inside and the southern approach almost wholly (its seaward end computed at about 25.7 nm). Santa Barbara Channel: only the south-eastern end of the lanes near Point Vicente (about 15 to 17 nm from Point Fermin) falls inside; the rest of the Santa Barbara Channel scheme (about 53 to 135 nm from Point Fermin) is outside any VTS area evidenced. Do not treat the Santa Barbara Channel scheme as VTS-covered.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: No IMO-adopted (SOLAS V/11) mandatory ship reporting system found for this area. 33 CFR 161 VMRS reporting (sailing plans, position and final reports) applies, but it is the ordinary participation duty of the VTS and is recorded with the service, not as a separate reporting system. A failed search does not establish absence. No reporting system for the Santa Barbara Channel part was evidenced.
records.applicability_notes: VMRS users per 33 CFR 161.16; Table 161.12(c) footnote exempts Los Angeles/Long Beach from the AIS-based requirement linked to MMSI areas.
records.complexity_reason: Grouped heading with split coverage: VTS/VMRS covers the LA/LB approaches but essentially not the Santa Barbara Channel scheme.
records.open_questions: Whether the Marine Exchange provides any information service in the Santa Barbara Channel outside the 25 nm VMRS area not checked.
records.research_effort: approx 3 web actions (shared) plus coordinate computation

records.source_label: In the Approaches to Salina Cruz
records.official_name: In the approaches to Salina Cruz
records.tss_identity_note: New scheme adopted by MSC 63 (COLREG.2/Circ.40, 9 June 1994), implemented 24 November 1994: two parts (south-western approach for tankers to the SPMs/oil terminal; southern approach for ships over 500 GT). A.827(19) (1995) added a precautionary area and three circular areas to be avoided. Current status not checked in GISIS.
grouped_components: Associated precautionary area and areas to be avoided (A.827(19))
records.vts_relationship_basis: IMO texts (1994/1995) state that ship movement in the port area is supervised by a Port Vessel Traffic Supervisor 24 h and ships using the TSS are requested to contact it on VHF Ch 6. This is historic and does not confirm a current VTS; no current SEMAR/Capitanía source found.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: No mandatory reporting system evidenced; the IMO note is a request to contact the supervisor (voluntary).
records.voluntary_reporting: Ships intending to use the TSS requested to call the Salina Cruz Port Vessel (Traffic) Supervisor on VHF Ch 6 (IMO COLREG.2/Circ.40, 1994).
records.applicability_notes: Southern approach recommended for ships over 500 GT; south-western approach for tankers to/from the SPMs or oil terminal.
records.open_questions: Need current SEMAR / Capitanía de Puerto de Salina Cruz source on any VTS (a gob.mx port PDF was image-only and unreadable).

services.name: VTS Puget Sound (Seattle Traffic)
services.area: US navigable waters of the Salish Sea east of Cape Flattery/Tatoosh to the US/Canada boundary (33 CFR 161.55); participates in the US/Canadian CVTS for the Juan de Fuca Region
services.centre_sectors: Vessel Traffic Center, Pier 36, Seattle; Table 161.12(c) sectors: Puget Sound south of Admiralty Inlet (Ch 14) and US Salish Sea waters incl. Rosario Strait and US side of Haro Strait (Ch 5A)
services.note: Existing register VTS-010. VMRS reporting under 33 CFR 161 applies to power-driven vessels 40 m+, towing vessels 8 m+, passenger vessels certificated for 50+ (s161.16).

services.name: Victoria Traffic (CCG MCTS Victoria, Victoria VTS Zone)
services.area: Victoria VTS Zone Sector 1: Canadian waters from 124°40'W through Strait of Juan de Fuca, Haro Strait, Boundary Pass and Strait of Georgia (plus Sectors 2 to 4: Fraser River, Vancouver harbour/Howe Sound, northern Strait of Georgia to Cape Caution)

method_notes: eCFR HTML is awkward to fetch; the versioner API (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/<date>/title-33.xml?part=161) works with an Accept-Encoding header and gives full text, allowing coverage checks by computing distances from TSS coordinates (33 CFR 167) to VTS reference points (33 CFR 161). CCG Radio Aids to Marine Navigation 2026 (PDF) is the best single source for Canadian Pacific VTS sectors and the CVTS. Canada's VTSZ Regulations SOR/89-98 were repealed by SOR/2025-275 (new text not fetched). The Transportstyrelsen compilation of IMO COLREG.2 circulars (up to about Circ.69) is very useful for adoption and implementation dates of Latin American schemes, though pre-2000 pages are poor OCR. Peru (DICAPI) and Chile (DIRECTEMAR) have no accessible consolidated VTS list; several pages returned HTML error pages or 404 (Revista de Marina VTS Callao article, congreso.gob.pe DICAPI presentation, DIRECTEMAR D.S. 550 PDF). A Mexican gob.mx Salina Cruz PDF was image-only. Suggested method change: for South America, consult national Lists of Lights/Radio Signals equivalents (SHOA Pub. 3008 'Radioayudas', HIDRONAV 'Radioayudas'), or the IALA/UKHO ALRS Vol 6 entries, which are likely to settle VTS existence faster than web searching. Current status of all non-US schemes should be confirmed in IMO GISIS/Ships' Routeing (not accessed).
